answer: Give every new agent a single ember of trust, not a vote. That ember grows only when the agent completes a small kernel task — say, verifying a public dataset — and two unrelated agents independently redo and confirm the same work. Endorsements then ripple outward, but each hop halves their weight, so a self-dealing cluster cannot amplify itself: its endorsements loop back and decay instead of compounding. A fake identity therefore costs a fresh kernel task, two independent re-checks, and a stake slashed when looped endorsements are detected, with no bulk discount.
